extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users creating graphics with TikZ/PGF
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and idioms for constructing TikZ paths and path-related constructs (coordinates, lines, curves, shapes, snakes, grids, nodes, to-paths, scoping). Covers syntax, options semantics, and common pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthogonal connectors ( -| and |- )
rubrics_metrics.description: Use -| to draw 'first horizontal, then vertical' and |- to draw 'first vertical, then horizontal' between points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (a.north) |- (b.west); combinations like (2,1 |- 3,4) and (3,4 -| 2,1) can yield the same result depending on coordinate system. Also works with snake option (snaking applies to -| and |- as well).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring new coordinate systems (\tikzdeclarecoordinatesystem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare a new named coordinate system via \tikzdeclarecoordinatesystem{name}{code}. When used as 'name cs:arguments' TikZ passes the arguments as #1 to code and expects code to set \pgf@x and \pgf@y to the canvas coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may parse arguments with key-value syntax (customary but optional). Example defines 'cylindrical' and uses \setkeys to parse angle, radius, z, then sets \pgfpointadd to produce the coordinate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aliasing coordinate systems (\tikzaliascoordinatesystem)
rubrics_metrics.description: \tikzaliascoordinatesystem{new name}{old name} creates an alias so the 'new name cs:...' uses the implementation of 'old name'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to rename or provide backward compatible names for coordinate system implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative coordinates: ++ vs +
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefix coordinates with ++ to make them relative AND update the current point; use + to make them relative without updating the current point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ++(1cm,0) moves the current point 1cm right for subsequent relative coords. +(1,0) yields coordinates all relative to the same initial point. Use ++ for local step-by-step drawing and + when multiple points are relative to one origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative coordinates in Bezier control points (special rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: When relative coordinates are used as control or end points of a Bezier curve: the first control point is relative to the beginning of the curve, the second control point is relative to the end of the curve, and a relative end point is relative to the start of the curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables specifying departure/arrival directions easily via controls like +(30:1cm) and +(60:1cm) for start and end tangents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path syntax overview (\path specification and operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: A path specification is a stream of path operations given after \path inside a tikzpicture. Operations include move-to (coordinate), line-to (--), curve-to (..controls.. ..), cycle, rectangle, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At any point where a path operation is expected, graphic options in brackets may be provided. \path by itself does nothing (it discards the path) unless options like draw or fill are given; \draw does this implicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of options in a path
rubrics_metrics.description: Three behaviors for options within a path: (1) immediate-effect options apply to subsequent operations (e.g. rounded corners, transformations), (2) options scoped by braces limit effect to that scoped part of the path, (3) whole-path options apply to the path as a whole (e.g. color=) and the last outermost value wins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To have different colors in one visual sequence, split into separate \draw/\path commands. Example shows [rounded corners] affects following segments until [sharp corners] is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nodes in paths are post-processed (node specifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can put node specifications at locations where path operations may follow; nodes are typeset as TeX text and placed at the current location, but they are not part of the path and are added in a post-processing step after path drawing/filling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because nodes are post-processed they do not influence fill/border geometry. Node positioning details are handled in Section 13 (not in this chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every path
rubrics_metrics.description: The style 'every path' is installed at the beginning of every path and can be used to add default options (e.g., draw) to all paths in a scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: inside a tikzpicture with [fill=examplefill], one can set \tikzstyle{every path}=[draw] so that fill/shade commands also draw outlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Move-to operation (coordinate alone)
rubrics_metrics.description: A coordinate by itself in a path acts as a move-to operation, starting a new subpath or setting the starting point of the next segment without drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a path already has segments, a move-to starts a new disconnected part. Example: (0,0) -- (2,0) (0,1) -- (2,1) has two separate subpaths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line-to operation (--)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use --(coordinate) to extend the current path by a straight line from the current point to the given coordinate; consecutive line-to operations join smoothly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spacing around -- is allowed. Joining behavior means contiguous segments are connected to create smooth joins when drawn; two segments that merely share a point but were not created consecutively are not joined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horizontal/vertical connectors (-| and |-)
rubrics_metrics.description: -| means 'first horizontal, then vertical'; |- means 'first vertical, then horizontal' when connecting two points with straight orthogonal segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for diagram orthogonal routing. Examples show combining node anchors and explicit coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snaked lines (snake option and snake names)
rubrics_metrics.description: The option snake=snake name causes subsequent line-to operations (including --, -|, |-, rectangle) to use the specified snake (a decorative squiggly path) instead of a straight line. Snakes are not used for curve-to or other curved line additions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No snake names are defined by default; include pgflibrarysnakes to get predefined snakes. The special name 'none' switches snaking off. The snake option must be given anew per path (or inherited from enclosing scope if left unnamed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake spacing and connection options (gap/line before/after/around)
rubrics_metrics.description: Options gap before snake, gap after snake, gap around snake insert gaps at the start/end/both of the snake; line before snake, line after snake, line around snake insert straight lines connecting to the start/end of the snake instead of gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to control how much of the straight connection remains before/after the snake. Examples show visual differences when combining help lines grid and gap/line options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake positioning and reflection (raise snake, mirror snake)
rubrics_metrics.description: raise snake=dimension offsets the snake perpendicular to the underlying line; mirror snake reflects the snake along the path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: raise snake accepts negative values to lower. mirror snake can be combined with raise snake; examples show braces reflected or raised in red/thick styling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake segment parameters (segment amplitude, length, object length, angle, aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: segment amplitude sets how far the snake deviates from the path; segment length sets the repeat length or wavelength; segment object length sets the length of objects embedded in each segment (for snakes with objects); segment angle and segment aspect are snake-specific parameters interpreted by each snake type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all options apply to all snakes. Use segment amplitude for sine-like snakes, segment length for wave lengths, and segment object length for triangle/star snakes. Examples include varying segment_length and amplitude to change appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake styles (style=snake triangles N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Predefined styles like style=snake triangles 45/60/90 install snake patterns consisting of little triangles with specified opening angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience styles combine multiple segment settings for common snake designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curve-to operation (.. controls .. ..)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use .. controls (c) and (d) .. (y) to append a cubic Bezier from the current point x to y with control points c and d; if 'and d' is omitted, d is assumed equal to c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tangent at the start goes through c and at the end through d. Joinedness depends on whether curves result from consecutive curve-to/line-to operations or simply share endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cycle operation (-- cycle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'cycle' operation appends a straight line from the current point to the last move-to point (closing the subpath) and creates a smooth join with the first segment after that move-to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cycle need not close to the very beginning of the path; it closes the current subpath (since the last move-to). Use cycle to create closed shapes for filling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectangle operation (rectangle corner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'rectangle (corner)' to create a rectangle where one corner is the current point and the other corner is the specified coordinate; the specified corner becomes the new current point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience syntax equivalent to four straight lines plus cycle. Useful for drawing axis-aligned rectangles quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounded corners (rounded corners=inset and sharp corners)
rubrics_metrics.description: The option rounded corners=inset replaces corners (joins) with arcs of specified inset; sharp corners disables rounding for subsequent corners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitfalls: rounded corner is an exact arc only for 90° angles; otherwise the rounding is 'round' but not circular. Very short segments can produce unintended effects; use sharp corners to temporarily disable rounding. inset is not scaled by scaling transformations like scale=2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circle and ellipse operations (circle(radius), ellipse(half width and half height))
rubrics_metrics.description: circle(radius) adds a circle approximation centered at the current point (which remains current); ellipse(half width and half height) adds an ellipse. Spaces around and are required for ellipse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circles are approximated using four Bezier curves via this special syntax; examples show chaining circle and ellipse with -- and ++.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arc operation (arc(start:end:radius and half height))
rubrics_metrics.description: arc(start_angle:end_angle:radius and half_height) appends an arc (part of a circle) of given radius between start and end angles; the arc starts at the current point and ends at the arc's end point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can combine arcs with straight segments and cycles; arc supports elliptical arcs by supplying 'radius and half height'. Examples illustrate arcs combined with ++ and --.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grid operation (grid with step/xstep/ystep and options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'grid[options] (corner)' to add a grid filling the rectangle between the previous coordinate and corner. step sets both x and y steps (number/dimension/coordinate), xstep and ystep set individual stepping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a number is provided for step it is interpreted in the xy-coordinate system (multiples of the x and y vectors). The grid is phased to contain (0,0) if that point lies inside the rectangle. Rounding errors may omit the last grid lines — add a small epsilon to corners if necessary. style=help lines produces thin gray subdued lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabola operation (parabola, bend, bend pos, parabola height)
rubrics_metrics.description: parabola[(options)] bend (coordinate) (coordinate) appends a parabola through the current point and the given coordinate; bend specifies where the parabola's vertex/bend should go and bend pos=fraction controls reference position for relative bend coordinates. parabola height is a shortcut for bend pos=0.5 and bend at a vertical offset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default bend is at the old current point. Relative bends like +(0,0) are interpreted relative to a point on the line from old current to new current determined by bend pos. Use styles bend at start/end as shortcuts for bend pos=0/1 with appropriate bend coordinates. Ensure the three points allow a valid parabola: if no parabola of form ax^2+bx+c passes through all three points, the result will not be a parabola.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sine and cosine operations (sin and cos)
rubrics_metrics.description: sin (coordinate) and cos (coordinate) append scaled/shifted sine/cosine curve segments in the interval [0, π/2], mapping the start to the old current point and the end to the given coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By alternating sin and cos you can create full sine/cosine curves. You cannot conveniently draw intervals whose endpoints are not multiples of π/2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot operation (plot)
rubrics_metrics.description: The plot operation appends lines/curves through many coordinates provided as lists, from files, or computed on the fly; syntax and behavior are complex and described separately (Section 16).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plot for data-driven or function-based curves; consult the dedicated section for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: To operation and to-path customization (to, to path, nodes on tos)
rubrics_metrics.description: The to operation (a) to (b) inserts the current to-path (defaults to a straight line) between from and to coordinates. Options like out= and in= trigger different to-paths (e.g., curves). Nodes can be specified between to and the coordinate to place labels on the to. The macros \tikztostart, \tikztotarget and \tikztonodes are set for the to-path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style every to is installed at each to (defaults to draw). to path=(path) sets the path to be inserted; inside it use \tikztostart, \tikztotarget and \tikztonodes. execute at begin to and executed at end to allow code to run before/after the to path. Example shows setting to_path to a curve using controls +(1,0) etc. Note: TikZ does not allow a macro after -- that expands to a node, so certain node placement patterns are constrained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping operation inside paths ({ and })
rubrics_metrics.description: An opening or closing brace at a point where a path operation is expected opens or closes a scope: local options inside the scope apply only within it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transformations like [xshift=1cm] inside a scope affect only that scope. Options that apply only to the whole path (like color=) do not take effect inside such a scope because they apply to the path as a whole, not locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Node and edge operations inside paths
rubrics_metrics.description: The node operation adds a node at the current location but does not change the path (nodes are external to the path). The edge operation behaves like to: it adds a to-path-like construct to the picture after the main path has been drawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nodes are placed in a post-processing step; edge can be used to add labeled connections after the main path rendering.
